fill_in_the_blank.description: Find the words that fit a gap in a sentence, given the word on either side of it. "Wreak ___" gives havoc and vengeance. suggestions.description: The suggested words, most popular first. The autocomplete endpoint never carries metadata, so every field but the word and its score is empty.

items.description: One matching word, with whatever metadata was asked for.

definition_headword.description: Set only when the word is an inflected form: the base form the definitions were drawn from, e.g. "run" for "running".

definitions.description: The word's dictionary senses. Empty unless Definitions was asked for under Include.

items.description: One dictionary sense of the word.

definition.description: The definition itself, from Wiktionary or WordNet.

part_of_speech.description: The part of speech this sense belongs to: n, v, adj, adv or u for anything else. Null when the source did not say.

frequency_per_million.description: How often the word occurs per million words of English text, per Google Books Ngrams. Under 1 means it is rare. Null unless How common the word is was asked for under Include.

num_syllables.description: How many syllables the word has. Null unless Syllable count was asked for under Include, or a syllable filter was set.

parts_of_speech.description: The word's parts of speech, most common first: n (noun), v (verb), adj, adv, u (none of these) and prop (proper noun). Several appear when the word is ambiguous. Empty unless Part of speech was asked for under Include, or the part-of-speech filter was set.

pronunciation.description: How the word is said, in the International Phonetic Alphabet. Null unless Pronunciation was asked for under Include.

pronunciation_arpabet.description: The same pronunciation in Arpabet, the ASCII phoneme notation the CMU pronouncing dictionary uses. Null unless Pronunciation was asked for under Include.

score.description: How the result ranked, highest first. Datamuse says the number has no meaning of its own beyond the ordering, so compare scores within one result set and never across two.

tags.description: The raw tags Datamuse attached, kept so nothing is lost: the parts of speech, the pronunciations prefixed "pron:" and "ipa_pron:", the frequency prefixed "f:", and any internal markers. The fields above hold the same values, parsed.

word.description: The word or phrase itself. Popular multiword expressions such as "hot dog" are part of the vocabulary and come back space-separated.

description: Find the word you are reaching for. Datamuse searches 550,000 English words and phrases (and 500,000 Spanish ones) by meaning, sound, spelling or the company they keep: synonyms and antonyms, rhymes and near rhymes, homophones, the adjectives writers actually use for a noun, the words that follow or precede another in print, and the reverse dictionary that turns "ringing in the ears" into "tinnitus". Wildcard patterns solve crosswords and anagrams, the fill-in-the-blank search finds the word that fits between two others, and any word can be looked up for its definitions, pronunciation, syllable count and how common it is. Every search can be narrowed to a part of speech or a syllable count. No account or API key required.
